newsitem.title: CROATIA: KLM seeking ties with Croatia Airlines.
newsitem.headline: KLM seeking ties with Croatia Airlines.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Friday it planned to start talks in May with Croatia Airlines on cooperation that could lead to the Dutch airline taking equity in the Croatian carrier.
"We're looking for a deep cooperation on a partnership basis with Croatia Airlines," Teo Juric, KLM's manager for Croatia and Slovenia, told Reuters from his office in Zagreb.
"The first meeting to discuss this will be in the second half of May, involving Croatia Airlines and KLM's head office and its office in Zagreb," Juric said.
The partnership likely would begin with Croatia Airlines flying passengers on its flights to Amsterdam for KLM to carry to further destinations, he added.
Croatia Airlines later might feed passengers to KLM on other European routes from Zagreb, and KLM eventually might take equity in Croatia Airlines.
"I would like to see my national carrier (Croatia Airlines) as a real partner with KLM -- even aircraft-color-wise," Juric said, noting that he has worked for KLM in Zagreb for 28 years.
KLM has operated no flights to Zagreb since suspending services in 1991, following the start of ethnic fighting in former Yugoslavia, Juric said.

But the Dutch airline carries cargo on Tuesdays and Fridays between Linz, Austria, and Zagreb on trucks with roughly seven tonnes of capacity, he said. Cargo arriving in Linz continues to Amsterdam on daily military aircraft flights leased by KLM.
The truck service, operating for two-and-a-half years, brings roughly 10 tonnes of cargo a week to Zagreb and exports "a little less," Juric said.
If cooperation talks with Croatia Airlines are unsuccessful, KLM plans to start daily flights to Zagreb on Boeing B737-300 airplanes, Juric said.
"We are talking now about the flights starting at end of September or the beginning of October," Juric said. "We would start six days a week, not flying on Saturdays, and soon add the seventh day."
